note: Known scenic roads for Adventure moto Day ride (moto-day.js). Hand-made: each road's points come from the route server (Valhalla, OpenStreetMap roads) between its two ends and were checked to follow the named highway; 'why' is a short summary in our own words, 'src' its source. Add a road: its two ends (and a middle point if the router leaves the highway), route them, keep a point every ~15 km.

roads.why: Highway 99 along Howe Sound, past the Stawamus Chief and Shannon and Brandywine falls, to Whistler.
Highway 99 over the Coast Mountains, past Joffre Lakes and Duffey Lake, with steep grades and tight turns.
Highway 1 up the Fraser Canyon, through seven tunnels and past Hell's Gate.
Highway 3 through E.C. Manning Provincial Park and over Allison Pass.
A winding valley road past Fish Lake; the Sandon ghost town is a short side road.
A curvy lakeshore road on the east side of Kootenay Lake, to the Kootenay Bay ferry.
Highway 6 over Monashee Pass, down to the Needles cable ferry on Lower Arrow Lake.
Highway 33 through the hills and down the Kettle River valley by Beaverdell.
Highway 4 over the mountains, past Kennedy Lake, to Tofino and the west coast.
roads.note: A Parks Canada pass is needed to stop in the national park.

roads.why: Highway 20 down The Hill from Heckman Pass to the Bella Coola valley: a steep gravel section with switchbacks.
Highway 37A through a narrow valley past Bear Glacier, to Stewart.
Highway 1 over Rogers Pass in Glacier National Park.
roads.note: Avalanche control can close this highway in winter (DriveBC). A Parks Canada pass is needed to stop in the national park.

roads.why: Highway 93 from Radium through Sinclair Canyon and Kootenay National Park, over Vermilion Pass.
roads.note: A Parks Canada pass is needed to stop in the national park.

roads.why: Highway 12 along the dry benches high above the Fraser River.
Highway 8 along the Nicola River through dry hills and ranch land.
Highway 93 from Lake Louise to Jasper past glaciers, Peyto Lake, Bow Summit and the Columbia Icefield.
roads.note: A Parks Canada pass is needed to travel this road.

roads.why: The slower road beside Highway 1 between Banff and Lake Louise, past Johnston Canyon.
roads.note: Parks Canada closes parts of it to vehicles at some times of year. A Parks Canada pass is needed to stop in the national park.

roads.why: Highway 40 through Kananaskis Country and over Highwood Pass, about 2,200 m.
roads.note: Highwood Pass closes every winter, Dec 1 to Jun 15 (Alberta Parks). A Kananaskis Conservation Pass is needed to park in Kananaskis Country.

roads.why: Highway 22 through the foothills and ranch land, with the Rockies to the west.
The south end of the Dempster Highway, to Tombstone Territorial Park.
Highway 17 along Lake Superior through Lake Superior Provincial Park and past Agawa Bay.
Highway 60 through the lakes and forest of Algonquin Park.
roads.note: An Ontario Parks day permit is needed to stop in the park.

roads.why: Route 132 along the St. Lawrence shore, with steep hills down into the villages, to Gaspé.
Route 362 over the hills above the St. Lawrence, through Les Éboulements and Saint-Irénée.
The Cabot Trail through Cape Breton Highlands National Park, over French and MacKenzie mountains by the sea.
roads.note: A Parks Canada pass is needed to stop in the national park.

roads.why: Route 430 from Deer Lake into Gros Morne National Park, by Bonne Bay to Rocky Harbour and Cow Head.
roads.note: A Parks Canada pass is needed to stop in the national park.
